transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. I guess I came in because my sleep is just... it's all broken up now. I'll get off an overnight shift at work and just lie there in bed, wide awake. And then when I finally do manage to drift off, I wake up scared. I just feel like I never really rested at all.
Does your trouble sleeping mainly happen after your overnight shifts?

No, it's pretty much all the time now. It doesn't matter if I just worked an overnight shift or if I have the night off. I just lie there wide awake. And like I said, even when I do finally fall asleep, I wake up feeling terrified and just... completely exhausted, like I didn't sleep at all. My sleep is just totally broken.
When you wake up scared, is it because of a nightmare about something traumatic that happened to you?

No, it's not like that. I don't really have nightmares about anything traumatic or... anything that actually happened to me. It's just this overwhelming feeling of being scared when I wake up, but there's no specific dream or memory tied to it. I'm just suddenly awake and terrified.
When you wake up feeling terrified, do you remember a vivid dream?

No, I don't really remember any dreams at all. I just... I wake up and my heart is pounding, and I'm just so scared, but there's nothing in my head that I can point to and say, 'That's what scared me.' It's just the feeling.
When you wake up terrified like that, do you remember the episode clearly afterward?

I mean... I remember waking up. I remember sitting there in the dark feeling my heart pound, and just being really scared. But there isn't really an... episode, I guess? Like I said, there's no dream or anything before it. I just remember the feeling of being awake and terrified, and that's pretty much it.
When you're lying awake and can't fall asleep, is your mind filled with worry?

No, not really. I'm not laying there stressing about my job or bills or anything like that. It's more like... my mind is just kind of blank, or heavy. I just stare at the wall and I can't sleep, but there aren't really any specific thoughts or worries keeping me up.
When you wake up terrified, is your heart pounding?
Yeah, um... like I said before, it is. My heart is just pounding really hard in my chest when I wake up like that.
When these scary awakenings happen, do they usually happen in the first part of your sleep?

I'm not really sure. Um... I don't usually look at the clock when it happens. It's just dark in the room, so I don't really know if it's right after I fall asleep or later on in the middle of the night.
After one of these scary awakenings, do you usually have trouble remembering what happened during it?
No, not really. I remember it happening. I mean, I know I woke up scared and... I remember just laying there feeling terrified. So, no, I don't have a hard time remembering it.
When you wake up terrified, do you scream or cry out?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't scream or anything. I just wake up and I'm really scared, but I usually just lay there quiet.
If you stop working overnight shifts for a few days, does your sleep get better?

No, it doesn't really matter if I work or not. That's actually why I came in... my sleep is just all broken up now. Even if I get off an overnight shift, I still just lie there wide awake. And then when I finally do drift off, I have those scary awakenings and wake up terrified. I just feel like I never get any rest at all, no matter what my schedule is.
Does your work schedule rotate between different shifts, or is it always overnight?

It rotates. My agency actually changed me to rotating overnight shifts, along with a bunch of extra paperwork, about a year and two months ago. That's pretty much how long all of this has been going on.
Did your sleep problems start after your work changed to rotating overnight shifts?
Yeah, pretty much. Once they switched my schedule to those rotating shifts, that's when the sleep problems started. It just hasn't been right since then.
When you get a chance to sleep at night instead of during the day, do you sleep better?

No, not really. Like I was saying earlier, my sleep is just completely broken up at this point. It doesn't matter if it's day or night... I still just lie in bed wide awake. And if I finally do manage to drift off, I still wake up scared. I just never feel like I've rested at all, no matter what time it is.
Have you had a stretch of at least a week completely away from the rotating overnight shifts?
No, I haven't. I've pretty much been working that same rotating schedule the whole time. I haven't had a full week off from it at all.
On days when you have enough time and a good place to sleep, do you still have trouble sleeping?

Yeah, even then. That's actually the main reason I came in, because my sleep is just all broken up now. I can get off an overnight shift, come home to my own bed with plenty of time, and I still just lie there wide awake. And like I said before, when I do finally drift off, I just wake up scared. I feel like I never rested at all, even when I have a good place to sleep.
If you were able to stop the rotating overnight shifts for at least a week, do you think your sleep would return to normal?

I really don't think so. Like I've been saying, that's the whole reason I came in here—my sleep is just completely broken up now. I feel like even if I had a whole week off, I'd still just lie there wide awake. And then when I finally do drift off, I wake up scared. I just always feel like I never rested at all. So no, I don't think just stopping the shifts for a week would make it go back to normal at this point.
When your shifts rotate, does your sleep problem get worse specifically during the times your schedule changes?

Not really, no. It's just... it's bad all the time now. Like I was saying, it doesn't even matter if the schedule is changing or if I just got off an overnight shift. My sleep is just completely broken up regardless. I just lie there wide awake either way. And then, you know, when I do manage to drift off, I still wake up scared. I just never feel rested at all anymore, no matter what my shifts are doing.
